requirements.feature: Election Safety Restriction (log up-to-date check)
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want a candidate whose log is behind to never win an election, so a leader with an incomplete log can never overwrite committed entries.
gherkinSteps: Given a candidate whose log lags the current leader's log; When its RequestVote arrives elsewhere first; Then the vote is denied because the candidate's log isn't at least as up to date.

requirements.feature: Conflicting-Entry Truncation
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want a follower whose log diverges from the leader's corrected automatically, so every replica converges to the same log.
gherkinSteps: Given a follower with an entry at index N from an old term; When an AppendEntries request carries a different entry at index N; Then the follower truncates from index N onward before appending the leader's entries.

requirements.feature: Leader-Only-Commits-Own-Term Rule (Figure 8)
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want a leader to only commit entries replicated during its own term, so an entry from a prior uncommitted term can never be silently re-exposed as committed.
gherkinSteps: Given a leader whose matchIndex table reaches majority for an entry from an earlier term; When advanceCommitIndex evaluates that index; Then the entry is not committed unless a later same-term entry also reaches majority.

requirements.feature: Strict Apply Ordering (commitIndex vs lastApplied)
requirements.userStory: As a state-machine implementer, I want committed entries applied strictly in order with no gaps.
gherkinSteps: Given commitIndex advanced past lastApplied by several entries; When applyCommittedLocked runs; Then every entry from lastApplied+1 through commitIndex is applied one at a time, in order.

requirements.feature: Proposal Timeout with Ghost-Write Prevention
requirements.userStory: As an application caller, I want a timed-out proposal truncated from the log rather than silently committing later.
gherkinSteps: Given a leader isolated from quorum submits a proposal; When the propose timeout elapses without majority ack; Then the entry is truncated from the leader's own log and GimleRaftException is thrown.

requirements.feature: Chunked InstallSnapshot Transfer (Figure 13)
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want a far-behind follower to catch up via bounded-size snapshot transfer instead of replaying the entire log.
gherkinSteps: Given a follower's nextIndex has fallen below the leader's snapshot floor; When the leader's peer-sender loop runs; Then it sends the snapshot as sequential offset/done chunks, installed only once the final chunk arrives.

requirements.feature: Local Log Compaction / Snapshotting
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want the Raft log compacted once it grows past a threshold, so disk usage and startup replay time stay bounded.
gherkinSteps: Given the log has grown beyond SNAPSHOT_THRESHOLD past the current floor; When applyCommittedLocked finishes; Then a new StateStore snapshot is taken and every entry at or below the floor is discarded.

requirements.feature: Check-Quorum Leader Self-Demotion
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want a leader isolated in a minority partition to step down on its own without observing a higher term, while a leader that simply has not finished opening its peer connections yet is not mistaken for one.
gherkinSteps: Given a leader that has already reached a majority of peers; When the check-quorum window elapses with no successful RPC round trip; Then the leader steps down to follower on its own.

Given a newly elected leader whose first peer RPCs have not completed yet; When only the check-quorum window has elapsed; Then it stays leader until one full peer-RPC attempt could have finished or failed, and only then steps down.

requirements.feature: Etcd-Style Live Membership Change (AddServer/RemoveServer)
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want to grow or shrink the Raft cluster one server at a time while live.
gherkinSteps: Given a running 3-node cluster with a leader; When addServer is called for a new peer; Then a self-inclusive MembershipChange entry is replicated, and a subsequent mutation still commits once the new node acknowledges; a second membership change is rejected while the first is uncommitted.

requirements.feature: Non-Voting Learner & Automatic Promotion
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want a newly-added peer to join as a non-voting learner and only be promoted once caught up.
gherkinSteps: Given a newly-added peer far behind the leader's log; When added via addServer; Then it doesn't count toward quorum until its matchIndex is within the catch-up threshold, at which point it's automatically promoted via a replicated MembershipChange.

requirements.feature: Durable Raft Log Persistence
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want every log entry and the current term/vote to survive a process crash.
gherkinSteps: Given a node appends entries and votes; When restarted and RaftLog reopened; Then every persisted entry, term, and vote are recovered exactly as written.

requirements.feature: Raft Transport over Mutual TLS with Hot Cert Reload
requirements.userStory: As a security-conscious operator, I want Raft peer traffic authenticated by mutual TLS with hot cert reload.
gherkinSteps: Given a cluster configured for mTLS with a shared CA; When peers exchange RequestVote/AppendEntries/InstallSnapshot; Then election and replication succeed as in plaintext; a peer cert not signed by the CA is rejected; reloaded TLS material lets a fresh connection succeed without restart.

requirements.feature: Raft RPC Wire Codec
requirements.userStory: As a platform engineer, I want Raft RPCs and log entries encoded in a compact, adversarial-input-resilient binary format.
gherkinSteps: Given an arbitrarily-constructed RaftRpc; When written and read back via RaftCodec; Then the decoded value equals the original; a forged oversized/negative length prefix is rejected before allocation.

requirements.feature: Atomic Durable File Writes
requirements.userStory: As a platform engineer, I want whole-file state (the Raft term/vote pair, compaction snapshots) written via temp-file-plus-atomic-rename with fsync.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete. Scope narrowed by the etcd-shape persistence rework: per-resource state files no longer exist (the WAL carries per-mutation durability), so this idiom now covers exactly the whole-file replaces that remain -- term/vote and snapshot state/meta.
gherkinSteps: Given a write crashes between temp-file write and final rename; When later read; Then no torn or partially-written file is ever visible.

requirements.feature: Raft WAL Persistence Engine with Snapshot-Replay Recovery
requirements.userStory: As the Raft state machine, I want durability carried entirely by the Raft log -- an append-only, CRC-guarded segment WAL plus compaction snapshots -- with the in-memory store rebuilt on restart from snapshot restore plus committed-entry replay.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete. Reworked from the original YAML-file-per-resource write-through engine to etcd's persistence shape: StateStore is purely in-memory; RaftLog rides a segment-based WriteAheadLog (one fsync per appended record, explicit truncation records so a discarded suffix stays discarded across a crash, crash-torn tail discarded on open, any other damage refuses to load, whole-segment compaction under the snapshot floor); a freshly elected leader appends a no-op entry at its own term so committed entries re-apply immediately on a quiet cluster.
gherkinSteps: Given a single-node store with committed writes; When the process restarts against the same directory with an empty in-memory store; Then the snapshot restores at construction and the fresh leader's no-op entry re-applies every committed entry above the floor.
Given a crash tears the WAL's final record mid-append; When the log reopens; Then the torn tail is discarded, every acknowledged record survives, and appends continue.

requirements.feature: Full-State Snapshot / Restore
requirements.userStory: As the Raft state machine, I want a point-in-time snapshot installable wholesale on another replica.
gherkinSteps: Given a StateStore holding every resource kind; When snapshot() then restoreFromSnapshot on a fresh store; Then every kind (except leader-local heartbeats) is reproduced identically.

requirements.feature: Replicated Mutation Catalog (StateMutation)
requirements.userStory: As a platform engineer, I want every state-changing operation represented as one sealed, replicated mutation type applied identically on every replica.
gherkinSteps: Given a StateMutation; When applied via applyTo(store) on any replica after commit; Then the exact same StateStore call is invoked with the exact same arguments everywhere.

requirements.feature: Leader-Local Node Heartbeat Tracking
requirements.userStory: As a reconciler, I want node heartbeats handled outside the replicated Raft log so high-frequency traffic never inflates the log.
gherkinSteps: Given a leader receives a heartbeat via putHeartbeat; When a follower is asked for that node's heartbeat; Then the follower answers empty, while the leader answers with the observed heartbeat.

requirements.feature: Distributed Lease Coordination (Grant/Renew/Release)
requirements.userStory: As a control-plane replica, I want a leader-local, TTL-based lease primitive usable to build reconciler-leader election.
gherkinSteps: Given a free lease; When holder A acquires it, then B tries before it expires; Then A succeeds, B is denied, and B succeeds once the TTL expires.

requirements.feature: Per-Instance Lifecycle Event Log with Retention Cap
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a bounded, newest-first timeline of lifecycle events per instance.
gherkinSteps: Given an instance that has accumulated more than MAX_EVENTS_PER_INSTANCE events; When another event is appended; Then the oldest event is pruned; listInstanceEvents returns newest-first.

requirements.feature: Cluster-Wide Audit Trail with Filtering
requirements.userStory: As a security auditor, I want every authorization decision recorded to a cluster-wide, filterable, bounded audit trail.
gherkinSteps: Given events across different principals/resources/tenants; When listAuditEvents is called with filters; Then only matching events are returned newest-first, and concurrent appends never lose/duplicate/exceed the cap.

requirements.feature: Deployment Rolling-Update & Surge Bookkeeping
requirements.userStory: As a reconciler, I want in-flight rolling-update and surge state persisted per deployment so a reconciler restart resumes instead of duplicating.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: Covered indirectly by `RaftCodecTest` mutation round-trips — NONE direct StateStoreTest method found
gherkinSteps: Given a deployment mid-rolling-update with index 2 marked in flight; When the control-plane process restarts; Then getRollingIndices still reports index 2 as in flight.

requirements.feature: StatefulSet OrderedReady Index & Sticky Node Binding
requirements.userStory: As a StatefulSet operator, I want each ordinal index sticky-bound to the node it first lands on.
gherkinSteps: Given an index never placed before; When first placed on node A via putStatefulSetIndexNode; Then a later rolling-update replacement of that index is placed on node A again; the binding survives ordinary assignment removal, cleared only on permanent index removal.

requirements.feature: Node Cordon (Scheduler Exclusion Flag)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want to mark a node as "don't place anything new here" without evicting what's already running.
gherkinSteps: Given an uncordoned node; When cordoned; Then isNodeCordoned reports true and survives a reload; uncordoning clears it.

requirements.feature: Tenant Quota-Violation Flag Tracking
requirements.userStory: As a tenant administrator, I want a deployment's quota-violation status tracked as a level-triggered flag.
gherkinSteps: Given a deployment marked quota-violating; When putQuotaViolation is called again with violating=false; Then isQuotaViolating reports false and the file is deleted.

requirements.feature: RBAC Data Persistence (Roles, RoleBindings, Accounts)
requirements.userStory: As a cluster administrator, I want roles, role bindings, and console-login accounts stored as first-class replicated resources.
gherkinSteps: Given a custom Role, RoleBinding, and Account; When put and a fresh StateStore instance opened; Then all three round-trip identically.

requirements.feature: Client-Facing Store RPC with Leader Redirect & Follow
requirements.userStory: As a control-plane process, I want a StoreClient that reads from any replica but automatically follows a NotLeader redirect for writes.
gherkinSteps: Given a StoreClient with no known leader; When propose() is called and a follower answers NotLeader with the real leader's address; Then the client retries directly against that address and caches it.

requirements.feature: Store Read Load Balancing Across Replicas
requirements.userStory: As a control-plane process, I want reads spread round-robin across every configured store endpoint, skipping unreachable ones.
gherkinSteps: Given three endpoints, one unreachable; When several reads are issued; Then each read tries endpoints from a rotating cursor and returns from the first reachable one.

requirements.feature: Store Node Leader-Only Write Gating
requirements.userStory: As a Raft node, I want every mutating RPC rejected with a leader-hint redirect if this node isn't leader.
gherkinSteps: Given a non-leader StoreNode; When it receives Propose/PutHeartbeat/AcquireOrRenewLease/AddServer; Then it responds NotLeader, carrying the leader's address if known, without applying anything.

requirements.feature: Store Client Connection Timeout Bounds
requirements.userStory: As a control-plane process, I want a connection that accepts but never responds to time out rather than hang forever.
gherkinSteps: Given an endpoint that accepts but never writes a response; When a StoreClient call is made; Then it fails with SocketTimeoutException within the configured bound, not indefinitely.

requirements.feature: Store RPC Wire Codec
requirements.userStory: As a platform engineer, I want the client-facing StoreRpc protocol encoded compactly and defensively.
gherkinSteps: Given any StoreRpc request/response; When written and read back through StoreCodec; Then the decoded value equals the original exactly.

requirements.feature: RBAC Authorization Engine
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a single authorizer combining explicit RoleBindings, an implicit cluster-admin operator group, and node self-service (its own node/log endpoints, plus cluster-wide read-only access to the Service and NetworkPolicy sets every node agent needs to relay/proxy).
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `AuthorizerTest#a_principal_with_no_binding_and_no_group_is_denied_everything`, `#an_operator_group_member_is_allowed_everything_via_the_implicit_cluster_admin_binding`, `#a_custom_role_bound_to_a_user_grants_exactly_its_declared_permissions`, `#a_tenant_scoped_permission_only_matches_its_own_tenant`, `#a_node_may_act_on_its_own_node_and_log_endpoints_with_no_role_binding_at_all`, `#a_node_is_denied_another_nodes_endpoints`, `#a_binding_referencing_a_role_that_no_longer_exists_grants_nothing`, `#a_node_may_read_the_cluster_wide_service_and_network_policy_sets_with_no_binding_at_all`, `#a_node_may_never_write_or_delete_a_service_or_network_policy`; `ApiServerNodeServiceAndNetworkPolicyAuthzTest` (`gimle-controlplane`) exercises the same grant through the real mTLS/RBAC HTTP layer.
gherkinSteps: Given a principal with a custom role bound to a declared permission set; When authorize is called for an action within it; Then allowed; outside it, denied; a group:gimle:operators member is always allowed everything; a gimle:nodes principal may act on its own node/log endpoints with no RoleBinding needed, and may always read (never write or delete) the cluster-wide Service and NetworkPolicy sets regardless of its own tenant assignments.

requirements.feature: Node-Tenant Assignment Check
requirements.userStory: As a security-conscious operator, I want a node agent's identity to only read a tenant's data if it currently hosts at least one instance for that tenant.
gherkinSteps: Given a node with an active instance for tenant "acme"; When isTenantAssignedToNode is checked; Then true; for an unassigned tenant, false.

requirements.feature: Five-Field Cron Schedule Evaluator
requirements.userStory: As a CronJob author, I want standard 5-field cron expressions evaluated correctly, including the day-of-month/day-of-week OR quirk.
gherkinSteps: Given a cron expression restricting both day-of-month and day-of-week; When mostRecentDueInstant is evaluated; Then a moment matching either restricted field counts as due; an invalid expression is rejected at parse time.

requirements.feature: Deployment Manifest Parsing (incl. Autoscale & Disruption Budget)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a Deployment manifest's replicas/placement/autoscale/rolling-update budget validated and parsed at submission time.
gherkinSteps: Given a manifest with a weighted autoscale block; When DeploymentManifestParser.parse is called; Then a DeploymentSpec carrying the exact weighted AutoscalePolicy is produced; maxUnavailable=0 with no maxSurge is rejected.

requirements.feature: DaemonSet Manifest Parsing (Anti-Affinity/Surge Rejection)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a DaemonSet manifest to reject anti-affinity and nonzero surge outright.
gherkinSteps: Given placement.antiAffinity: true; When DaemonSetManifestParser.parse is called; Then parsing throws; a nonzero disruption.maxSurge is likewise rejected while 0 is accepted.

requirements.feature: Job / CronJob Manifest Parsing
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want Job and CronJob manifests parsed with sensible defaults and validated cron schedules.
gherkinSteps: Given a minimal CronJob manifest with no explicit backoffLimit; When parsed; Then defaults are applied and an invalid cron schedule/unknown concurrencyPolicy is rejected.

requirements.feature: StatefulSet Manifest Parsing
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a StatefulSet manifest parsed with the same placement/tenant/vessel shape as other kinds.
gherkinSteps: Given a manifest declaring replicas/placement/a vessel block; When parsed; Then a StatefulSetSpec is produced; zero replicas is legal, negative rejected.

requirements.feature: Kind-Dispatching Manifest Parser
requirements.userStory: As an API server, I want one entry point that reads a manifest's `kind:` field and dispatches to the right parser.
gherkinSteps: Given a manifest with kind: Deployment; When ManifestParser.parse is called; Then it dispatches to DeploymentManifestParser; an unrecognized kind is rejected via GimleManifestException.unknownKind.

requirements.feature: Shared Domain Binary Codec
requirements.userStory: As a platform engineer, I want domain types encoded once and shared between the Raft wire format and the client RPC wire format.
gherkinSteps: Given a DeploymentSpec carrying an optional VesselSpec; When encoded via DomainCodec and decoded back; Then the result equals the original, including the absent-vessel case.

requirements.feature: Store Process Bootstrap with TLS Rotation Ticker
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want the store process to wire up Raft node/RPC transports and a periodic cert-rotation check on startup.
gherkinSteps: Given a store process started with a state dir, Raft port, client port; When it starts up; Then it constructs StateStore/RaftLog/RaftNode, binds both transports, and rotates its own cert if due.

requirements.feature: Store/Raft Metrics Instrumentation
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want per-RPC-kind request/error/latency metrics recorded for the store's client-facing RPC handling.
gherkinSteps: Given a client RPC request handled by StoreNode; When it completes; Then StoreMetrics records the kind, duration, and error status exactly once.

requirements.feature: module-info JPMS Boundary for gimle-mimir
requirements.userStory: As a platform engineer, I want gimle-mimir's public surface explicitly exported and dependencies declared.
gherkinSteps: Given the gimle-mimir module descriptor; When another module requires com.gimle.mimir; Then it can access authz/cron/manifest/store/raft/rpc, nothing unexported.

requirements.feature: Same-Worker Direct Invocation Tier
requirements.userStory: As a hosted module, I want a service call to a provider in my own worker JVM served as a direct in-JVM method call.
gherkinSteps: Given a service registered in the same worker's local registry; When lookup(Class) is called; Then the local registry's instance is returned directly, bypassing the catalog entirely.

requirements.feature: Same-Machine Unix-Domain-Socket Invocation Tier
requirements.userStory: As a hosted module, I want a call to a provider in a different worker on the same machine dispatched over a Unix domain socket.
gherkinSteps: Given a provider in a different worker on the same node; When lookup resolves to that endpoint; Then the call is dispatched over a UDS (always plaintext).

requirements.feature: Cross-Machine TCP Invocation Tier
requirements.userStory: As a hosted module, I want a call to a provider on a different machine dispatched over TCP (optionally TLS).
gherkinSteps: Given a provider on a different node's worker; When lookup resolves to that endpoint; Then the call is dispatched over TCP, TLS when configured.

requirements.feature: Locality-Aware Load Balancing with Spillover
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want the fabric to prefer same-machine endpoints but spill into remote once every same-machine candidate is busier than the least-loaded remote one.
gherkinSteps: Given several same-machine endpoints saturated and a remote endpoint with spare capacity; When lookup selects a candidate; Then the remote tier is admitted; when a same-machine endpoint is idle, remote is never consulted.

requirements.feature: Least-Outstanding-Requests Selection
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want traffic within a candidate tier routed to the endpoint with fewest outstanding requests, ties broken round-robin.
gherkinSteps: Given two candidates, one busier; When select is called; Then the less-loaded candidate is chosen; ties round-robin.

requirements.feature: Per-Endpoint Circuit Breaker
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want each remote endpoint protected by its own sliding-window error-rate circuit breaker.
gherkinSteps: Given an endpoint's error rate crosses errorRateThreshold; When another call is attempted; Then the breaker opens and excludes it; after cooldown it half-opens for one trial call.

requirements.feature: Circuit Breaker Exponential Cooldown Backoff
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want each consecutive re-open to double the effective cooldown (capped at 16x).
gherkinSteps: Given a breaker that re-opens repeatedly; When each re-open occurs; Then the cooldown doubles up to a ceiling; a successful half-open trial resets it.

requirements.feature: Panic-Mode Ejection Floor
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want lookup to stop excluding open-breaker endpoints once more than a configured fraction are ejected.
gherkinSteps: Given a lookup whose candidates are more than maxEjectionPercent open-breaker; When selectAllowedCandidate runs; Then every candidate is admitted back in; no known exporter anywhere still throws GimleClusterException.

requirements.feature: Application-Exception vs Transport-Failure Breaker Scoring
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a remote method's own thrown exception counted as a successful (reachable) call for breaker purposes.
gherkinSteps: Given a remote endpoint whose method throws an application exception; When the call completes with InvokeError; Then the breaker records a success; only genuine transport failures count against it.

requirements.feature: Gossip-Propagated Service Catalog
requirements.userStory: As a node agent, I want every locally-registered service export propagated cluster-wide over the SWIM gossip channel, never through the control plane.
gherkinSteps: Given a local registration on one catalog; When its payload is applied to a second catalog's onReceived; Then the second reflects the registration; a stale delta at a lower version is ignored.

requirements.feature: Catalog Eviction on Gossip-Detected Node Death
requirements.userStory: As a caller, I want a node's catalog entries proactively hidden the moment SWIM converges on it as DEAD.
gherkinSteps: Given a member gossip converges on as DEAD; When ServiceCatalog#onMembershipChange receives it; Then endpointsForInterface no longer returns any of its endpoints; once ALIVE again, endpoints reappear with no re-registration.

requirements.feature: Cross-Tenant Service Export Access Control
requirements.userStory: As a multi-tenant platform operator, I want a service export's `allowedTenantIds` allow-list enforced at lookup time, with opt-in default-deny for unscoped exports.
gherkinSteps: Given an export restricted to tenant "acme"; When a caller from a different tenant looks it up; Then lookup returns empty; with defaultDenyCrossTenant on, an unscoped export is reachable only by an untenanted caller.

requirements.feature: Runtime Name-Driven Cross-Tier Invocation (invokeByName)
requirements.userStory: As a gateway module resolving routes at runtime, I want to invoke a service by interface name/version/method rather than a compile-time Class<T>.
gherkinSteps: Given a route naming an interface/version/method/param types; When invokeByName is called; Then it resolves the same tier/breaker/tenant logic dispatched by name; an unresolvable method name fails clearly.

requirements.feature: Inbound Call Dispatch with Bounded Concurrency
requirements.userStory: As a worker JVM, I want inbound fabric calls routed through the target module's own bounding scheduler.
gherkinSteps: Given a target module with a bounded ModuleWorkExecutor; When more concurrent inbound calls arrive than allowed; Then extra calls queue; ModuleContext's in-flight counter reflects real inbound calls.

requirements.feature: Distributed Trace Propagation Across Fabric Hops
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a caller's OpenTelemetry span/baggage propagated across a cross-worker or cross-machine fabric call.
gherkinSteps: Given a caller with an active span and baggage; When it invokes a remote service; Then the callee starts a child span parented on the caller's real span, observing the same baggage.

requirements.feature: Fabric Transport over Mutual TLS with Hot Cert Reload
requirements.userStory: As a security-conscious operator, I want cross-machine fabric calls authenticated by mutual TLS, hot-reloadable.
gherkinSteps: Given fabric configured for mTLS; When a cross-machine invocation is made; Then it succeeds over TLS; a client trusting a different CA is rejected; reload lets a fresh connection succeed without restart.

requirements.feature: Fabric Call Timeout Enforcement
requirements.userStory: As a caller, I want a cross-hop call bounded by one overall timeout regardless of transport.
gherkinSteps: Given a peer that accepts but never responds; When FabricClient.call is made; Then it fails with SocketTimeoutException within the bound; a refused connection fails fast.

requirements.feature: Fabric Frame Wire Codec
requirements.userStory: As a platform engineer, I want cross-hop invocation requests/responses encoded compactly and defensively.
gherkinSteps: Given a FabricFrame.InvokeRequest with tracestate/baggage; When written and read back through FabricCodec; Then the decoded frame equals the original; forged length/param counts are rejected before allocating.

requirements.feature: Cross-JVM Object Marshalling
requirements.userStory: As a platform engineer, I want method arguments/return values/exceptions serialized via plain Java serialization for cross-hop calls.
gherkinSteps: Given an object graph as a fabric method argument; When serialize then deserialize is applied; Then the result is an equivalent object graph, trusted only within the same platform trust boundary (no ObjectInputFilter allowlist).

requirements.feature: SWIM Gossip Membership Protocol (Ping/PingReq/Ack)
requirements.userStory: As a node agent, I want cluster membership tracked via SWIM's ping/indirect-ping/ack protocol independent of the control plane.
gherkinSteps: Given two node agents configured with each other as a seed; When they join; Then each discovers the other via direct ping/ack; a killed member converges to DEAD via direct probe timeout escalating to indirect PingReq relays.

requirements.feature: SWIM Self-Refutation via Incarnation Bump
requirements.userStory: As a node being falsely suspected, I want to automatically refute the suspicion by gossiping a higher incarnation of myself.
gherkinSteps: Given a member observes a piggyback entry naming itself as SUSPECT; When processed; Then it bumps its own incarnation and re-gossips as ALIVE; a stale suspicion below the current incarnation is ignored.

requirements.feature: Lifeguard-Style Local Health Multiplier
requirements.userStory: As a cluster, I want a node whose own probes keep timing out to scale up its own timeouts, so it doesn't flood the cluster with false suspicions.
gherkinSteps: Given a node whose probes repeatedly time out; When each timeout occurs; Then its local health multiplier increases (clamped at a ceiling); a successfully resolved probe decays it back down.

requirements.feature: Round-Robin Bounded-Coverage Probe Target Selection
requirements.userStory: As a cluster, I want every live member probed at least once per protocol-period cycle.
gherkinSteps: Given N live members besides self; When N consecutive ticks each call nextProbeTarget; Then every live member is visited exactly once before the queue reshuffles.

requirements.feature: Anti-Entropy Full-State Sync
requirements.userStory: As a cluster, I want a periodic full-membership-table push-pull sync so a lagging node still eventually converges.
gherkinSteps: Given a change piggyback alone never delivered to a lagging node; When the antiEntropyInterval elapses and a sync fires to a random peer; Then the full table is exchanged and the lagging node picks up the missed change.

requirements.feature: Dead-Member Reaping
requirements.userStory: As a cluster, I want a member DEAD longer than a configured window forgotten from the membership table.
gherkinSteps: Given a member DEAD longer than deadMemberReapAfter; When the next tick's reapExpiredDeadMembers runs; Then the member is removed entirely.

requirements.feature: Gossip over Mutual DTLS with Deterministic Initiator Selection
requirements.userStory: As a security-conscious operator, I want gossip UDP traffic encrypted/authenticated via DTLS when TLS mode is configured.
gherkinSteps: Given two nodes configured for DTLS gossip; When they exchange pings; Then they discover each other over mutual DTLS, with only the lexicographically-lower-addressed side originating the handshake; different-CA members never become mutually aware; reloaded material lets a node reach a new peer.

requirements.feature: SWIM Wire Codec
requirements.userStory: As a platform engineer, I want SWIM protocol messages encoded compactly over UDP with defensive bounds against malformed datagrams.
gherkinSteps: Given any SwimMessage variant; When encoded and decoded via SwimCodec; Then the decoded value equals the original; a forged huge piggyback count or unrecognized protocol version fails cleanly.

requirements.feature: Service Catalog Delta Wire Codec
requirements.userStory: As a platform engineer, I want catalog deltas encoded defensively so a forged delta count can't force unbounded allocation.
gherkinSteps: Given a list of CatalogDelta values; When encoded/decoded via ServiceCatalogCodec; Then the round trip is exact; a forged huge delta count fails cleanly.

requirements.feature: Reflective Cross-Module Method Dispatch
requirements.userStory: As the fabric transport, I want to resolve and invoke a wire-carried interface/method/parameter-type triple against a module-private service interface without a shared platform-layer classloader.
gherkinSteps: Given an inbound call naming an interface/method/param types belonging to a module-private interface; When ReflectiveDispatch resolves and FabricServer invokes it; Then it resolves against the instance's own declaring interface, avoiding IllegalAccessException.

requirements.feature: module-info JPMS Boundary for gimle-fabric
requirements.userStory: As a platform engineer, I want gimle-fabric's public surface explicitly exported and its dependency on gimle-module explicit.
gherkinSteps: Given the gimle-fabric module descriptor; When gimle-worker requires com.gimle.fabric; Then it can access cluster/catalog/registry/transport/balance/breaker/trace, nothing unexported.

requirements.feature: First-fit-decreasing bin-packing scheduler
requirements.userStory: As a control-plane operator, I want instances placed on the node with the most free capacity among feasible candidates, so that cluster load stays balanced without manual placement.
gherkinSteps: Given multiple registered nodes with differing free memory/CPU; When a replica is placed for a deployment; Then the node with the most free memory (tie-broken by free CPU) among tier-eligible, uncordoned nodes is chosen.

requirements.feature: Isolation-tier placement filtering
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want instances only scheduled onto nodes that support the requested isolation tier, so that Tier 2/3 guarantees are never silently downgraded.
gherkinSteps: Given a node that does not declare support for TIER_2; When a TIER_2 replica is placed; Then that node is excluded and placement fails if no other node supports the tier.

requirements.feature: Node cordon exclusion
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want to mark a node as unschedulable without evicting what's already running there, so I can drain it safely for maintenance.
gherkinSteps: Given a node marked cordoned; When a new replica needs placement; Then the cordoned node is excluded from candidacy, but its existing instances are untouched.

requirements.feature: Strict anti-affinity across nodes
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want replicas of one deployment spread across distinct nodes when anti-affinity is requested, so a single node failure can't take down every replica.
gherkinSteps: Given anti-affinity is requested and every eligible node already runs a replica; When another replica is placed; Then placement fails outright rather than co-locating.

requirements.feature: Tier 2/3 node-level tenant isolation
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want Tier 2/3 instances from different tenants kept off the same node, so compliance-sensitive workloads get physical separation.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete (documented one-directional asymmetry across other reconcilers' tenant checks, not a bug)
gherkinSteps: Given a node already running Tier 2 instances for tenant A; When a Tier 2 replica for tenant B is scheduled; Then that node is excluded; if every candidate hosts a different tenant, placement fails outright.

requirements.feature: Required node-label placement constraint
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want to require a deployment land only on nodes carrying specific labels, so hardware/location-specific workloads reach the right machines.
gherkinSteps: Given a manifest declares placement.requiredLabels; When placement runs; Then only nodes carrying every required label are candidates; fails outright if none qualify.

requirements.feature: StatefulSet sticky node placement
requirements.userStory: As an operator running a stateful workload, I want each replica index to always return to the same node once placed there, so its local-disk volume is never orphaned.
gherkinSteps: Given index 3 was previously placed on node-A; When index 3 needs re-placement; Then it is placed on node-A again if eligible, and fails outright (never relocated) if node-A is unavailable.

requirements.feature: DaemonSet eligible-node enumeration (`eligibleNodes`)
requirements.userStory: As an operator running a DaemonSet, I want it placed on every eligible node cluster-wide rather than bin-packed onto one.
gherkinSteps: Given several nodes, some cordoned, some missing required labels; When DaemonSetReconciler computes eligible nodes; Then every node passing tier/cordon/tenant/label filters is returned, no single-winner pick.

requirements.feature: Deployment replica reconciliation (level-triggered)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want actual running instances to always converge to my declared replica count, regardless of prior history.
gherkinSteps: Given a deployment declares 3 replicas and only 1 assignment exists; When DeploymentReconciler ticks; Then 2 more are placed; an arbitrary starting snapshot converges to the identical result a fresh reconcile would produce.

requirements.feature: Deployment scale-down
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want reducing replica count to immediately remove excess assignments.
gherkinSteps: Given 5 assignments and replicas lowered to 3; When DeploymentReconciler ticks; Then assignments for indices 3 and 4 are removed.

requirements.feature: Artifact-hash drift detection at reconcile time
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want the reconciler to refuse new placements if a deployment's on-disk artifact no longer matches the hash recorded at admission.
gherkinSteps: Given a deployment admitted with artifactSha256 recorded; When the jar is later swapped for different bytes; Then no new instance is placed until resubmitted.

requirements.feature: Rolling update via mismatched-index migration
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want deploying a new module version to gradually replace old-version instances up to `maxUnavailable` at a time.
gherkinSteps: Given 5 running old-moduleId instances and disruption.maxUnavailable=1; When the spec's moduleId changes; Then exactly 1 index is replaced at a time, waiting for readiness before the next.

requirements.feature: Rolling update surge (maxSurge)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a rollout to optionally provision replacement instances before tearing down old ones, so the deployment never drops below its declared count.
gherkinSteps: Given disruption.maxSurge=1 and an old-version instance at index 2; When a rollout starts; Then a synthetic surge index is placed with the new version, promoted onto index 2 once ready, and the old assignment removed.

requirements.feature: Node-death instance reclamation (`ReplicaCountReconciler`)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want an instance whose node has gone dark to be released for re-placement after a grace period.
gherkinSteps: Given an assignment's node hasn't heartbeated within nodeDarkTimeout, persisted beyond placementGracePeriod; When ReplicaCountReconciler ticks; Then the assignment is removed, freeing re-placement.

requirements.feature: Persisted grace-period bookkeeping (survives leader failover)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want the "how long missing" timer to survive a reconciler-leader failover, so a fresh leader doesn't restart the grace period.
gherkinSteps: Given an instance missing for half of placementGracePeriod when the leader lease changes hands; When the new leader reconstructs from the store; Then it resumes counting from the persisted timestamp, not zero.

requirements.feature: Unhealthy-instance backoff-gated reschedule (`HealthReconciler`)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want an instance reported unhealthy to be rescheduled with exponential backoff, so a persistently crashing replica isn't bounced in a tight loop.
gherkinSteps: Given an instance's heartbeat reports alive=false or lifecycleState=FAILED; When HealthReconciler ticks; Then it is rescheduled after growing delay; once maxAttemptsPerWindow is exhausted it's marked permanently failed.

requirements.feature: Readiness-only failures never trigger reschedule
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a not-yet-ready instance left running rather than torn down.
gherkinSteps: Given an instance reports ready=false but alive=true and lifecycleState != FAILED; When HealthReconciler ticks; Then no reschedule action is taken.

requirements.feature: Tenant quota drift detection (`QuotaReconciler`)
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a deployment marked quota-violating whenever its tenant's actual usage exceeds quota, without automatic eviction.
gherkinSteps: Given a tenant's quota is lowered below already-running usage; When QuotaReconciler ticks; Then affected deployments are marked quota-violating with no instances evicted.

requirements.feature: Horizontal autoscaling — multi-signal (`AutoscaleReconciler`)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want replica count to auto-adjust based on CPU, request rate, error rate, and queue depth.
gherkinSteps: Given a policy targeting CPU and queue depth, WORST_SIGNAL mode; When queue depth implies more replicas than CPU; Then effective count moves toward the worst signal's ideal, one replica per tick, clamped to [min,max].

requirements.feature: Autoscaling WEIGHTED combination mode
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want to blend multiple autoscale signals into one weighted ratio instead of taking the worst.
gherkinSteps: Given combinationMode=WEIGHTED with per-signal weights; When two signals disagree; Then effective count is driven by the weighted-average blended ratio.

requirements.feature: DaemonSet reconciliation and rolling update
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a DaemonSet's per-node instance kept in sync with eligible nodes and rolled forward on version changes.
gherkinSteps: Given an old module version on 3 nodes; When the spec's moduleId changes; Then nodes migrate one at a time, waiting for readiness.

requirements.feature: DaemonSet dark-node placement-safety grace period
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a briefly-partitioned node's assignment left alone rather than torn down.
gherkinSteps: Given a node's heartbeat is stale but within nodeDarkTimeout+placementGracePeriod; When DaemonSetReconciler ticks; Then the assignment is left in place.

requirements.feature: StatefulSet OrderedReady placement
requirements.userStory: As an operator running a stateful workload, I want index i+1 never placed until index i reports ready.
gherkinSteps: Given index 0 is not yet ready; When StatefulSetReconciler ticks; Then index 1 is never placed.

requirements.feature: StatefulSet one-index-at-a-time scale-down
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want scaling down to remove exactly one (highest) index per tick.
gherkinSteps: Given 5 indices and replicas lowered to 2; When StatefulSetReconciler ticks; Then only index 4 is removed this tick.

requirements.feature: JobRun run-to-completion reconciliation
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a Job to run to completion with automatic retry up to backoffLimit.
gherkinSteps: Given a Job's current attempt fails and backoffLimit allows another; When JobReconciler ticks; Then a new attempt is placed; once exhausted, the Job is marked FAILED.

requirements.feature: Job active-deadline enforcement
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a Job running longer than its activeDeadline forcibly marked failed.
gherkinSteps: Given activeDeadline=10min and the run has been active 11min; When JobReconciler ticks; Then the run is removed and the Job marked FAILED mid-attempt.

requirements.feature: CronJob schedule-driven Job materialization
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a CronJob's schedule to automatically materialize a real Job at each due time.
gherkinSteps: Given a CronJobSpec with schedule "* * * * *" and no prior lastSchedule; When first ticked; Then baseline is recorded with no retroactive burst; on the next due tick a Job named "{name}-{epochSeconds}" is materialized.

requirements.feature: CronJob concurrency policy (Allow/Forbid/Replace)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want to control overlapping CronJob firings via concurrency semantics.
gherkinSteps: Given the previous firing is still non-terminal and concurrencyPolicy=FORBID; When a new firing is due; Then it is skipped and logged.

requirements.feature: CronJob manual trigger (`gimle cronjob trigger`)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want to fire a CronJob on demand independent of its schedule.
gherkinSteps: Given a CronJob exists; When POST /cronjobs/{name}/trigger is called; Then a Job is materialized immediately, and cronJobLastSchedule is left untouched.

requirements.feature: CronJob missed-schedule starting-deadline handling
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a too-late firing skipped rather than run stale, so an outage doesn't cause a burst of overdue runs.
gherkinSteps: Given a firing's startingDeadline is exceeded by processing time; When CronJobReconciler ticks; Then the firing is logged as missed with no Job materialized.

requirements.feature: Level-triggered orphan cleanup across every workload kind
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want deleting a workload spec to automatically clean up its stale assignments on the next tick.
gherkinSteps: Given a deployment is deleted but its assignments remain; When the reconciler ticks; Then every assignment is removed.

requirements.feature: Reconciler-leader election via non-replicated lease
requirements.userStory: As an operator running multiple control-plane replicas, I want exactly one replica actively reconciling at a time.
gherkinSteps: Given multiple ApiServer replicas share one store cluster; When each replica's leaseTick runs; Then only the lease-holder executes the reconcile tick.

requirements.feature: Independent-executor ticking (lease/reconcile/cert-rotation isolation)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a slow reconcile tick to never block certificate rotation or lease renewal.
gherkinSteps: Given the reconcile tick is deliberately blocked forever; When cert rotation and lease renewal keep ticking on their own executors; Then both continue unaffected.

requirements.feature: JPMS module boundary for gimle-controlplane
requirements.userStory: As a maintainer, I want the control plane's public API surface explicitly exported and dependencies explicitly declared.
gherkinSteps: Given module-info.java for com.gimle.controlplane; When compiled/linked with jlink; Then only schedule/reconcile/api/pki/top-level packages are exported.

requirements.feature: Admission chain extension point
requirements.userStory: As a platform maintainer, I want admission checks run as an ordered, pluggable chain rather than hardcoded inline.
gherkinSteps: Given a chain with a rejecting plugin followed by an allowing plugin; When admit() runs; Then processing short-circuits at the first rejection; a later plugin sees an earlier plugin's mutated spec.

requirements.feature: Tenant resource quota admission check
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a Deployment, Job, DaemonSet, or StatefulSet submission rejected outright if it would push its tenant past its quota (accounting for surge headroom on a Deployment, and each kind's own peak committed-instance count via WorkloadResourceProfile).
requirements.statusDetail: Complete -- generalized from Deployment-only to every placeable WorkloadSpec kind (Deployment/Job/DaemonSet/StatefulSet) so a tenant can no longer bypass its quota by submitting a Job/DaemonSet/StatefulSet instead of a Deployment.
gherkinSteps: Given tenant T's quota is nearly exhausted; When a submission with maxCommittedInstances (replicas+maxSurge) would exceed it; Then admission rejects with 409.

requirements.feature: Organization-specific policy-as-data admission (`policy.maxReplicasPerDeployment`)
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a per-tenant ceiling on replicas-per-deployment via ordinary config.
gherkinSteps: Given tenant T has policy.maxReplicasPerDeployment=10; When a submission requests 15 replicas; Then admission rejects citing the ceiling.

requirements.feature: Registry-coordinate artifact admission (Andvari integration)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a coordinate-only deployment admitted only if Andvari confirms the artifact exists.
gherkinSteps: Given a manifest names moduleId:version with no artifactPath, and Andvari doesn't have it; When submitted; Then admission rejects with 400; if Andvari is merely unreachable, admission still accepts with no recorded digest (level-triggered tolerance).

requirements.feature: PUT-time re-tenanting double-authorization
requirements.userStory: As a platform security owner, I want moving a resource between tenants to require write access under both tenants.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: Embedded in `ApiServerAuthzTest`'s broader RBAC flow coverage
gherkinSteps: Given deployment D belongs to tenant A; When a caller with write access only to tenant B PUTs D with tenantId=B; Then the request is rejected unless the caller also has write access to tenant A.

requirements.feature: RBAC-gated resource CRUD across every workload kind
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want every workload resource gated by an independent RBAC check per verb.
gherkinSteps: Given a principal with no grant for ResourceKind.JOB; When GET/PUT/DELETE against /jobs/{name}; Then every request is rejected with 403.

requirements.feature: WRITE/DELETE decisions durably audited (opt-in READ auditing)
requirements.userStory: As a compliance auditor, I want every WRITE/DELETE decision recorded, and READ optionally audited per resource kind.
gherkinSteps: Given -Dgimle.controlplane.audit.readResourceKinds=CONFIG,SECRET; When a READ hits /config/* or /secrets/*; Then an AuditEvent is durably appended even for allowed reads.

requirements.feature: `gimle-system` reserved-tenant operator-only guard
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want the reserved `gimle-system` tenant accessible only by `gimle:operators`-group callers.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: Exercised within `ApiServerAuthzTest`'s broader RBAC test set
gherkinSteps: Given a caller holds a broad but non-operator-group grant; When writing under tenantId=gimle-system; Then rejected 403 regardless of ordinary RBAC outcome.

requirements.feature: Node-scoped self-service authorization (`gimle:nodes` group)
requirements.userStory: As a node agent, I want to reach only my own node's subresources with no explicit RoleBinding needed.
gherkinSteps: Given a certificate carrying gimle:nodes and CN=node-42; When calling POST /nodes/node-42/heartbeat; Then it succeeds via the self-service short-circuit; a request against node-99 is rejected.

requirements.feature: Node-tenant-scoped `/endpoints/*` read access
requirements.userStory: As a node agent, I want to read service-discovery endpoint data only for tenants my node currently hosts an assignment for.
gherkinSteps: Given node-42 has an active instance for tenant T; When it calls GET /endpoints/{workload-of-T}; Then access is granted; a request for a tenant it has no assignment for is rejected 403.

requirements.feature: mTLS-authenticated HTTP API server with client-cert principal resolution
requirements.userStory: As a platform security owner, I want every control-plane API call authenticated by client cert under TLS mode, falling back to session cookie for the console.
gherkinSteps: Given gimle.transport.protocol=tls and a CA-signed client cert; When any request is made; Then the principal is resolved from the certificate subject; absent a cert, a session cookie is checked.

requirements.feature: Console session login/logout/session cookie flow
requirements.userStory: As a human operator, I want to log in with username/password and get a signed session cookie.
gherkinSteps: Given a valid bootstrap Account; When POST /auth/login with correct credentials; Then a signed, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict session cookie is set.

requirements.feature: Login throttling (address + username keyed)
requirements.userStory: As a platform security owner, I want repeated failed logins throttled independently by username and address.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: Exercised via shared `LoginThrottle` mechanics (`FafnirObservabilityTest`'s equivalent); no isolated ApiServer-level test method found
gherkinSteps: Given repeated failed logins for the same username from different addresses; When the username-keyed threshold is exceeded; Then further attempts are throttled with 429+Retry-After.

requirements.feature: Bootstrap node join via single-use token + CSR
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a freshly-provisioned node to join via a one-time bootstrap token and a CSR.
gherkinSteps: Given an operator issued a bootstrap token; When a new node submits a CSR (purpose=NODE_CLIENT) with that token; Then the CA signs a cert stamped O=gimle:nodes, and the token cannot be reused.

requirements.feature: Operator-approval-gated CSR flow
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a human operator's CSR to require an existing operator's explicit approval.
gherkinSteps: Given a human submits a CSR (purpose=OPERATOR_CLIENT) with no client certificate; When submitted; Then it sits pending (202) until an existing operator approves it.

requirements.feature: Certificate rotation (self-rotation and subject-preserving renewal)
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a certificate renewable before expiry using its own still-valid certificate, preserving its exact prior subject.
gherkinSteps: Given a caller presents its own still-valid cert with a matching-subject rotation CSR; When submitted; Then a new cert is issued for the identical subject; a mismatched subject is rejected 403.

requirements.feature: Zero-downtime TLS material reload
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a certificate rotation to take effect without restarting the control-plane process.
gherkinSteps: Given the control plane's cert is rotated; When reloadTlsMaterial runs; Then the HttpsServer is rebuilt with new key material and a fresh connection succeeds.

requirements.feature: `/secrets/*` byte-for-byte proxy to Fafnir
requirements.userStory: As a client, I want to interact with the versioned secrets API without knowing Fafnir runs as a separate process.
gherkinSteps: Given a caller has WRITE access to SECRET for tenant T; When PUT /secrets/T/mykey; Then ApiServer authorizes locally, forwards byte-for-byte to Fafnir with the calling principal as an internal claim, and relays the response verbatim.

requirements.feature: Secrets key rotation trigger (proxied)
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want to trigger secrets master-key rotation and have every encrypted entry re-encrypted.
gherkinSteps: Given several encrypted entries exist; When POST /secrets/rotate-key; Then Fafnir generates a new key, re-encrypts every entry, and every previously-encrypted secret still decrypts.

requirements.feature: CONFIG/SECRET resource-kind separation on one underlying store
requirements.userStory: As a platform security owner, I want plain config and encrypted secrets independently RBAC-gated even though they share one store.
gherkinSteps: Given a caller has CONFIG:WRITE but not SECRET:WRITE; When PUT /config/{tenant}/{key} with encrypted=true; Then the write is rejected because it routes authorization through ResourceKind.SECRET.

requirements.feature: `/artifacts/*` streaming proxy to Andvari
requirements.userStory: As a client, I want to push/pull/list module jars through the control plane's single API surface.
gherkinSteps: Given --andvari-endpoint is configured; When a caller with ARTIFACT:WRITE PUTs a jar; Then ApiServer authorizes locally and streams the jar straight through, never buffered whole.

requirements.feature: Andvari-client multi-endpoint failover with rotation
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator running multiple Andvari replicas, I want reads to automatically fail over on transport failure.
gherkinSteps: Given two configured endpoints, the first unreachable; When a HEAD request is made; Then it transparently retries against the second endpoint.

requirements.feature: `/logs/*` proxy with Muninn fallback
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want log requests to fall through to Muninn when the owning agent/node is gone.
gherkinSteps: Given an instance's owning node is unregistered or unreachable, and Muninn is configured; When a caller requests logs; Then ApiServer falls through to Muninn instead of 404/502.

requirements.feature: `/metrics-history/*` and `/traces-history/*` Muninn proxy
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want to query historical metrics/traces for any process kind through the control plane.
gherkinSteps: Given Muninn is configured; When a caller with LOGS:READ requests /metrics-history/{processKind}/{processId}?since=...; Then the request is proxied to Muninn.

requirements.feature: Node registration, heartbeat, and assignment-fetch API
requirements.userStory: As a node agent, I want to register capabilities, send heartbeats, and fetch my current assignment set.
gherkinSteps: Given a node agent starts up; When it POSTs /nodes/{id}/register then periodically /nodes/{id}/heartbeat; Then the control plane records capacity/observations, usable by GET /nodes/{id}/assignments.

requirements.feature: Unified `AssignedInstance` wire shape across every workload kind
requirements.userStory: As a maintainer, I want Job/DaemonSet/StatefulSet/Deployment assignments all mapped onto one wire shape.
gherkinSteps: Given a node has a mix of assignment kinds; When GET /nodes/{id}/assignments; Then every kind is represented uniformly as AssignedInstance entries.

requirements.feature: Reserved system-tenant auto-seeding
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want the reserved `gimle-system` tenant to always exist with generous quota, seeded automatically.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: Implicit in test fixtures bootstrapping ApiServer
gherkinSteps: Given a fresh control-plane replica starts against an empty store; When it initializes; Then it proposes a Tenant row for RESERVED_SYSTEM_TENANT_ID unless one already exists.

requirements.feature: Bundled web console static serving
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want the control plane to serve its own bundled web console at /console with zero extra deploy steps.
gherkinSteps: Given the console/index.html resource is present on the classpath; When ControlPlaneMain starts; Then it serves the bundled SPA at /console with client-side-route fallback.

requirements.feature: Per-endpoint request metrics instrumentation
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want every API route's request count, latency, and error rate tracked independently.
gherkinSteps: Given a request is made to any registered route; When the handler completes; Then request count/latency/error status are recorded, tagged by endpoint and verb.

requirements.feature: Deployment/Job/DaemonSet/StatefulSet CRUD manifest API
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want to submit, read, and delete declarative workload manifests via a uniform REST surface.
gherkinSteps: Given a valid Deployment manifest YAML; When PUT /deployments/{name}; Then GET returns the round-tripped spec, and DELETE removes it.

requirements.feature: Per-deployment and per-instance metrics rollup
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want request-rate/error-rate rollups per deployment surfaced through the API.
gherkinSteps: Given a deployment has 3 ready instances reporting different request rates; When GET /metrics; Then a per-deployment row with the averaged rates is returned.

requirements.feature: AES-256-GCM secret value encryption with versioned key IDs
requirements.userStory: As a platform security owner, I want every secret encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM tagged with which key encrypted it, so key rotation doesn't break decryption.
gherkinSteps: Given a secret encrypted under key id 3; When decrypted after the ring rotates to key id 5; Then decryption succeeds by looking up key id 3 from the embedded byte.

requirements.feature: Legacy pre-key-id ciphertext format fallback
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator upgrading an existing cluster, I want secrets encrypted before key-rotation existed to still decrypt correctly.
gherkinSteps: Given a blob encrypted before the version/keyId prefix existed; When decrypt() runs; Then the new-format decode fails GCM verification and falls back to the legacy iv||ciphertext layout under key id 0.

requirements.feature: Local AES-256 key-file generation and loading
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want Fafnir to generate its own master key file on first run with owner-only permissions.
gherkinSteps: Given no key file exists; When KeyFileManager.loadOrCreate runs; Then a fresh key is generated, written rw-------, and reused on later loads.

requirements.feature: Key rotation with full-ring persistence (`KeyFileManager.rotate`)
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want rotating the key to generate a new key while keeping every previous one loadable.
gherkinSteps: Given a ring holding key id 0; When rotate() runs; Then a new key id 1 file is written, .active repointed, key id 0 remains loadable.

requirements.feature: Key-ring fingerprinting for cross-replica drift detection
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator running multiple Fafnir replicas, I want a safe-to-log fingerprint of each replica's key ring.
gherkinSteps: Given two replicas hold identical key material in different map order; When fingerprint() is computed; Then both produce the identical SHA-256 hex digest.

requirements.feature: Full-key-rotation re-encryption sweep
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want every existing encrypted config entry re-encrypted under the newly-rotated key.
gherkinSteps: Given several tenants have encrypted entries under the old key; When FafnirCrypto.rotate() runs; Then every encrypted entry is re-encrypted under the new key.

requirements.feature: Versioned secret storage layered over ConfigEntry
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want secrets stored with full version history, not just the latest value.
gherkinSteps: Given a secret key written 3 times; When GET /secrets/{tenant}/{key}/versions; Then versions 1,2,3 are all listed and independently retrievable via ?version=N.

requirements.feature: Optimistic-write versioned put with narrow-lease serialization
requirements.userStory: As a platform maintainer, I want concurrent writes to never produce duplicate version claims.
gherkinSteps: Given two writers race to PUT the same key; When both complete; Then exactly one version number is claimed by each, serialized via a narrow lease around the final @meta-advance step.

requirements.feature: Soft delete vs hard delete (`?destroy=true`)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want soft-delete by default (recoverable) and hard-delete only when explicitly requested.
gherkinSteps: Given a key with 3 versions; When DELETE without ?destroy=true; Then hidden from default GET but every version remains individually readable; with ?destroy=true, every version is permanently removed.

requirements.feature: Fafnir's own independent RBAC re-check (defense-in-depth)
requirements.userStory: As a platform security owner, I want Fafnir to never trust a proxied "already authorized" claim from the control plane.
gherkinSteps: Given a forwarded principal claims access but doesn't actually hold the permission; When Fafnir independently re-checks Authorizer.authorize; Then denied with 403 regardless of the forwarder's decision.

requirements.feature: Node-tenant-scoped secret reads (`gimle:nodes`)
requirements.userStory: As a node agent, I want to read a tenant's secrets directly from Fafnir only for a tenant I currently host an assignment for, never write/delete.
gherkinSteps: Given node-42 has an active assignment for tenant T; When it reads GET /secrets/T/{key}; Then granted; PUT/DELETE, or reading an unassigned tenant, is rejected.

requirements.feature: Authorization-failure throttling and dual audit logging
requirements.userStory: As a platform security owner, I want repeated authz failures throttled, and every /secrets/* decision durably audited.
gherkinSteps: Given a principal repeatedly fails authorization; When the failure count crosses the threshold; Then further requests are throttled with 429+Retry-After.

requirements.feature: Three-tier principal resolution (forwarded header > peer cert > session cookie)
requirements.userStory: As a maintainer, I want Fafnir to correctly identify the true calling principal regardless of arrival path.
gherkinSteps: Given a request carries both a forwarded header and its own peer cert; When resolvePrincipal runs; Then the forwarded header wins.

requirements.feature: mTLS HTTP server with dynamic TLS material reload
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want Fafnir's certificate rotation to take effect without a process restart.
gherkinSteps: Given Fafnir's cert is rotated; When reloadTlsMaterial runs; Then a fresh mTLS connection using the new cert succeeds without restart.

requirements.feature: Console session login (Fafnir's own operator dashboard)
requirements.userStory: As a human operator, I want to log in to Fafnir's own console independent of the control plane's console.
gherkinSteps: Given a valid Account; When logging in via Fafnir's /auth/login; Then a distinct gimle_fafnir_session cookie is issued.

requirements.feature: Plaintext-mode anonymous session carve-out

gherkinSteps: Given a fresh metrics wrapper (e.g. ApiServerMetrics) with an in-memory SimpleMeterRegistry
When recordRequest(endpoint, verb, latency, error=true) is called
Then the latency Timer, the count Counter, and the errors Counter are all incremented/recorded
And requestCount/errorCount return 0 for a tag combination never recorded
And different endpoint/verb (or ModuleId, or rpcKind) combinations are tracked independently

requirements.feature: WorkerMetrics thread-count / metaspace gauges
requirements.userStory: As a worker JVM, I want live gauges of per-module thread count and metaspace footprint (not cumulative counters), so a periodic metrics report reflects each module's current, not historical, resource footprint.
gherkinSteps: Given WorkerMetrics.recordThreadCount(moduleId, 5) then recordThreadCount(moduleId, 9)
When the gauge is read
Then it reflects 9 (the latest value), not the first recorded value

requirements.feature: Fafnir authz-failure counter (rate-limiting signal)
requirements.userStory: As Fafnir, I want a verb-tagged (not principal-tagged) counter of consecutive authorization failures, so `LoginThrottle`-based rate limiting on `/secrets/*` has a bounded-cardinality signal to key off regardless of fleet size.
gherkinSteps: Given a FafnirMetrics instance
When recordAuthzFailure("GET") is called
Then gimle.fafnir.authz.failures{verb=GET} increments
And authzFailureCount for an unrecorded verb returns 0

requirements.feature: Muninn endpoint list parsing from config
requirements.userStory: As a process reading `-Dgimle.agent.muninnEndpoint`-style config, I want a comma-separated address list parsed into a normalized endpoint list (trimmed, blanks dropped, single-address backward compatible), so multi-replica Muninn shipping is configurable via one property.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: NONE found as a dedicated test (only exercised indirectly via multi-endpoint shipping tests that construct `MuninnShipper` with an already-parsed `List<String>`)
gherkinSteps: Given a config value of "host1:9090, host2:9090,,host3:9090"
When MuninnShipper.parseEndpoints(value) is called
Then it returns ["host1:9090", "host2:9090", "host3:9090"], trimmed and blanks dropped
And a null/blank value returns an empty list

requirements.feature: Fabric-route HTTP-to-service dispatch
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want an HTTP path to invoke a named fabric service method by interface/version/method name, so external HTTP traffic can reach a hosted module's service without that module exposing its own listener.
gherkinSteps: Given a FabricRoute "/greet" bound to interface Greeter, version 1, method "greet", ParamType.STRING
When a POST /greet request arrives with body "Gimlé"
Then ModuleContext#invokeServiceByName is called with the coerced argument
And the response is 200 with the real return value as plain text

requirements.feature: Fabric-route argument coercion (`ParamType`)
requirements.userStory: As a route author, I want a route's single argument type declared (NONE/STRING/INT/LONG/DOUBLE/BOOLEAN) and its plain-text HTTP body coerced accordingly, so a malformed request body is rejected cleanly rather than propagating a raw parse exception.
gherkinSteps: Given a FabricRoute with ParamType.INT
When a request body that isn't a valid integer is POSTed
Then the response is 400 with a message naming the expected type
And a NONE-typed route is only ever served on GET; every other type is served on POST

requirements.feature: Vessel-route HTTP reverse-proxy dispatch
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want an HTTP path to reverse-proxy verbatim (method, path, body) to a live instance of a named deployment's named port, so I can front any HTTP-speaking Gimlé deployment through one gateway without the gateway understanding its protocol.
gherkinSteps: Given a VesselRoute "/api/orders" -> deployment "orders-service", port "HTTP_PORT"
When a PUT /api/orders request with a JSON body arrives
Then a resolved live instance receives the same method, path, and body unchanged
And the gateway's response is exactly that instance's status and body

requirements.feature: Vessel-endpoint resolution with TTL cache
requirements.userStory: As the gateway, I want a deployment's live endpoint list cached for a bounded TTL rather than refreshed via a relay round trip on every request, so the gateway itself never becomes the latency bottleneck.
gherkinSteps: Given a resolved endpoint list cached at time T with TTL=5s
When resolve() is called again before T+5s
Then no new relay call is made (cache hit)
When resolve() is called after T+5s
Then a fresh relay call is made

requirements.feature: Round-robin load balancing over ready vessel endpoints
requirements.userStory: As the gateway, I want repeated requests to a vessel route spread round-robin across every endpoint that reports both a host and the named port, so no single instance absorbs all traffic.
gherkinSteps: Given two ready endpoints for a deployment
When four consecutive requests are dispatched
Then both endpoints are hit, alternating in round-robin order
And an endpoint missing the named port or missing a host is never selected

requirements.feature: Stale-cache fallback on endpoint-refresh failure
requirements.userStory: As the gateway, I want a failed endpoint refresh (non-2xx relay response, or an unparsable body) to fall back to the still-cached endpoint list when one exists, so one bad refresh doesn't fail every in-flight request to a previously-healthy deployment.
gherkinSteps: Given a cached endpoint list from a prior successful refresh
When the TTL expires and the next refresh returns 504
Then resolve() still returns the previously-cached Ready endpoint, with a warning logged
But if no list was ever cached and the refresh fails, resolve() returns Unavailable

requirements.feature: Vessel-route error surfacing (no ready endpoint / connect failure)
requirements.userStory: As a client of a vessel route, I want a clear error status (not a misleading 200) when a target deployment has no ready endpoints or refuses the outbound connection, so I can distinguish "downstream unhealthy" from "call succeeded."
gherkinSteps: Given a deployment with zero live/ready endpoints
When a vessel route is dispatched
Then the response is 503
Given a resolved endpoint that refuses the TCP connection
When the proxy call is attempted
Then the response is a clean 502, not an uncaught exception

requirements.feature: Route-table config DSL parsing
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want gateway routes declared in a compact line-oriented text format (`FABRIC ...` / `VESSEL ...`) read from `gateway.routes` config, so routing behavior is fully config-driven with no code change per deployment.
gherkinSteps: Given a gateway.routes value mixing FABRIC and VESSEL lines, blank lines, and "#" comments
When GatewayRouteConfig.parse(text) is called
Then blank/comment lines are ignored and each remaining line becomes the correct route type
And a malformed line (wrong field count, unknown kind, bad majorVersion/paramType) throws GatewayConfigException naming the line number

requirements.feature: Duplicate route-path rejection at config-parse time
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want two routes (of either kind) declaring the same HTTP path rejected at config-parse time (module startup), rather than silently letting one shadow the other on request, so a config mistake fails fast and loudly.
gherkinSteps: Given a config with two lines both declaring path "/api/orders" (one FABRIC, one VESSEL, or same-kind duplicates)
When GatewayRouteConfig.parse is called
Then it throws GatewayConfigException before any route table is built

requirements.feature: Gateway HTTP server bootstrap via module lifecycle hooks
requirements.userStory: As the gateway module, I want its listen port and route table read from `ModuleContext#config(...)` and a plain `HttpServer` bound on `onStart`, torn down on `onStop`, so it participates in the platform's own module lifecycle rather than needing external process management.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: NONE found in `gimle-gateway/src/test/java` (no direct `GatewayHooks` test; only `GatewayDispatcher`/`GatewayRouteConfig`/`VesselEndpointCache` are unit-tested)
gherkinSteps: Given required config keys gateway.port and gateway.routes are present
When onStart(ctx) runs
Then an HttpServer binds on 0.0.0.0:{port}, one context per configured route, using a virtual-thread-per-task executor
And onStop() stops the server and flips readiness to false
And a missing/non-integer gateway.port throws GatewayConfigException before binding

requirements.feature: Gateway liveness and readiness probes
requirements.userStory: As the platform's self-healing supervisor, I want a liveness probe that's always true once loaded and a readiness probe gated on the HTTP listener actually being bound, so traffic isn't routed to a gateway instance before it can accept connections.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: NONE found (no dedicated probe test in `gimle-gateway`'s test tree)
gherkinSteps: Given GatewayHooks has not yet run onStart
Then GatewayReadinessProbe.isReady() returns false
When onStart completes successfully (port bound)
Then GatewayReadinessProbe.isReady() returns true
And GatewayLivenessProbe.isAlive() always returns true

requirements.feature: HTTP status-code error mapping across the dispatcher
requirements.userStory: As a gateway client, I want a consistent, never-throwing mapping of every known failure mode to an HTTP status (404 unknown path, 405 wrong verb, 400 bad body, 502 downstream failure, 503 no ready endpoint), so `GatewayDispatcher#dispatch` never requires its caller to catch an exception to produce a response.
gherkinSteps: Given a request to a path with no configured route
Then the response is 404
Given a fabric route invoked with the wrong HTTP verb
Then the response is 405
Given a downstream fabric call that throws
Then the response is 502

requirements.feature: Boot-only platform-layer JPMS workaround (`requires static`)
requirements.userStory: As the module system, I want `gimle-gateway` to declare `com.gimle.module`/`com.gimle.core`/`org.slf4j` as `requires static` rather than plain `requires`, so JPMS `Configuration.resolve` succeeds even though no real `gimle-api` platform module exists yet — resolution then relies on `ModuleLayerFactory` separately granting readability to the platform's unnamed module at runtime.
